blocks.title: Recipe: A Socratic Seminar (Serves Twelve)
paras: **Ingredients:** one short text; twelve curious people; a **pinch of doubt**; two **open-ended** questions; one chair per guest; **unlimited patience**. **Preparation time:** 20 minutes. **Seminar time:** 60 minutes.

**Method.** **Arrange** the chairs in a circle. **Read** the text aloud, **then let it rest** for a full minute. **Pose** your first question and **resist** the urge to answer it. **Season to taste** with follow-ups: “What do you mean by…?” **Simmer** until two guests disagree **politely**. **Serve** with an exit slip. **Do not** hurry; the dish is **spoiled** by **tidy conclusions**.

items.q: The leader should answer the first question immediately.
items.why: resist the urge to answer it.

items.q: The recipe says a tidy conclusion improves the seminar.

blocks.body: Receitas usam **imperativos curtos**, **quantidades** (*a pinch of*, *one … per guest*) e **tempos**. O tom é firme: a voz **cai** em cada comando (↘). Ao dar uma dica, a voz **sobe** levemente (↗).
*Serves twelve* (porções) ≠ *serves as* (funciona como). Atenção à preposição em *serve with*.

body: **Stir the pot.** — Mexer em vespeiro.
**Let it simmer.** — Deixar fermentar.
**Too many cooks.** — Cozinheiros demais.
**A recipe for disaster.** — Receita para o desastre.
**Half-baked idea.** — Ideia mal cozida.
**Food for thought.** — Algo para refletir.
**Add fuel to the fire.** — Jogar lenha na fogueira.
**Take with a grain of salt.** — Receber com ressalvas.
**On the back burner.** — Em banho-maria.
**Cook up a storm.** — Preparar com fartura.
**Do I answer the first question myself?** — Eu mesmo respondo à primeira pergunta?
**And when do I step in?** — E quando intervenho?
**No. Resist the urge, and let it rest.** — Não. Resista ao impulso e deixe descansar.
